source_validation.scope: source geometry, contacts and explicit opening hosts

assumptions: Correction cell rings represent physical source spaces with horizontal floor/ceiling boundaries.
Contacts describe adjacency, not traversability or EnergyPlus surface pairing.
Only explicit openings are represented; absent observations do not establish a solid wall.
Source boundary identity follows cell identity and ring order; topology edits need identity migration.

Interior corridor/office door heights (F1:D1-D6, F2:D1-D6) remain an explicit assumption of 2.1m, matching the elevation-evidenced exterior entrance doors (F1:D7, F1:D8) and confirmed window-head pattern; these 12 interior doors are not directly visible in any supplied elevation (interior partitions are not elevated) and remain unlinked to image height evidence in check_openings.

West wall vestibule/porch recess (~1m deep, corridor width) simplified to a flush exterior wall with a single wide entrance door D7 spanning the corridor width; the small projecting porch geometry itself is not modeled.
South wall small notch/chamfer near the SW entrance simplified to a flush wall with a single door D8.
All door swing/open states left unknown.
Plan spaces were compiled deterministically from the declared footprint and physical partition segments; no snapping, extension, clipping, or inferred partition was applied.
No exterior ground-level door assumed on 2F (upper storey); vertical circulation (stair) is not shown in the supplied plan/elevation views and is not modeled.
All door swing/open states left unknown.
Plan spaces were compiled deterministically from the declared footprint and physical partition segments; no snapping, extension, clipping, or inferred partition was applied.

scope.endpoint_selection: exact original image name and linked wall floor

limits: Endpoint pixels are the declared original-image evidence and are drawn without inferred movement.
Tangential range and normal displacement are conditional on the caller-supplied axis-aligned calibration.
A dimension extension-line tick may legitimately lie outside its linked finite wall segment; this is a spatial fact, not an error or correctness verdict.
This view does not inspect pixels, choose a host wall, or mutate source geometry or evidence.

input_view_status.note: Only this run's hash-bound direct original returns from view_image or paired elevation views are counted. Other image tools, workers and prior runs are outside this scope. A returned image is not proof of examination, complete coverage, correct interpretation or applied heights. Use supplied relevant elevations to check each floor's opening heights; do not transfer a typical height to an unexamined opening family.

room_use_review.next_action: Read room_types and edits, inspect original room interiors, then use revise_bim/set_space_role to choose a plausible use, including a reasonable inference from building context. Prefer a broad listed type over unknown; avoid spending excessive effort distinguishing similar plausible uses. Read remaining cells with read_candidate_items; preserve physical partitions.
room_use_review.interpretation: Counts cover structured role_evidence only, not semantic correctness. Legacy source_refs may contain other evidence. Unknown remains a fallback when no defensible listed use fits; it is not a preferred response to ambiguity.

decision.reason: Dimension chain matches built window family within 7mm; confirms independent elevation evidence for F1 typical windows.

claims.reason: North elevation (and matching South/East labels) show, below the F1/F2 floor line, a vertical dimension chain of 400/1600/1000 mm reading top-to-bottom from the floor line (absolute z=3.0m) down to ground. The middle 1600mm segment is the standard F1 office window (all typical single windows on north, south offices b/c, and east corridor). Segment index 1 (0-based) of a chain starting at origin 3.0m walking down (direction -1) gives absolute z=[1.0,2.6]m, matching the built [1.007,2.605].

decision.reason: Dimension chain matches built F2 window family within 12mm; confirms independent elevation evidence.

claims.reason: North elevation (matched on South/East/West) shows, above the F1/F2 floor line, a vertical dimension chain of 800/1800/1000 mm reading top-to-bottom from the roof/wall-top (absolute z=6.6m) down to the floor line. The middle 1800mm segment is the typical F2 window (conference rooms, offices, corridor east/west windows). Segment index 1 of a chain starting at origin 6.6m walking down (direction -1) gives absolute z=[4.0,5.8]m, matching the built [4.012,5.801].

decision.reason: Dimension chain matches built small south window within 9mm; confirms independent elevation evidence.

claims.reason: South elevation shows, below the F1/F2 floor line, a vertical dimension chain of 900/600/1500 mm (top-to-bottom from floor line z=3.0m to ground) specifically over the small window next to the south entrance door (office_1f_south_a). Segment index 1 (the 600mm window) of a chain starting at origin 3.0m walking down (direction -1) gives absolute z=[1.5,2.1]m, matching the built [1.509,2.098].

unresolved: Intermediate tick at pixel~428 for the 1F window-head was not directly matched by the automated colour scan (obscured by the '400' label); it is inferred from the dimension-chain arithmetic (division 405 + 400mm) and cross-checked against the East_view.png family which used the same split.

Bottom frame line at pixel y=482 had weak isolated pixel support (count=2) in the raw color-run output; the outer rectangle bottom edge is still clearly visible in the enlarged crop view_0011/view_0013.
